title: Analyzing and Reducing the Performance Gap in Cross-Lingual Transfer with Fine-tuning Slow and Fast
why: Analyzes catastrophic forgetting in cross-lingual transfer fine-tuning, unrelated to coding-agent design-constraint compliance or cost frontiers.

title: Tell2Design: A Dataset for Language-Guided Floor Plan Generation
why: A dataset for language-guided architectural floor-plan generation; 'design' here means building layout, not software architecture/dependency-direction rules, so it is unrelated to coding-agent design-constraint compliance.

title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
why: The execution-verified coding-agent benchmark substrate (fail-to-pass tests) this paper's utility axis is built on; digest N3/N4.1 grounded, but not in the harvested 150-candidate cache, so added directly to close the integrity gap.

title: RECAST: Expanding the Boundaries of LLMs' Complex Instruction Following with Multi-Constraint Data
why: Closest overlapping estimand (constraint-satisfaction under verifiable rewards) but trains for NL-constraint satisfaction without a joint pass-rate/cost frontier (digest N4.2); requires concede-and-differentiate treatment in Related Work.

title: Self-Play with Execution Feedback: Improving Instruction-Following Capabilities of Large Language Models
why: Establishes the 'constraint checker as executable code' pattern this paper's M3 checker inherits, but measures satisfaction rate alone with no utility/cost axis (digest N4.2); shares RECAST's limitation and needs concede-and-differentiate treatment.

title: Syntactic and Semantic Control of Large Language Models via Sequential Monte Carlo
why: Explicit compute-for-compliance enforcement-mechanism precedent (particle reweighting for expensive semantic constraints) informing M2's enforcement-arm design and the mechanism-vs-constraint cost split (C4), but evaluates satisfaction/fidelity, not a swept strength-cost-pass-rate frontier (digest N4.4).

title: Mitigating the Safety Alignment Tax with Null-Space Constrained Policy Optimization
why: Names the 'alignment tax' analogue this paper's motivation cites as adjacent evidence that utility-compliance trade-offs are real elsewhere, but for training-time safety alignment, not inference-time design-constraint enforcement in coding agents (digest N2, N4.5).

title: Robust Multi-Objective Controlled Decoding of Large Language Models
why: Decode-time Pareto/multi-objective framing precedent for characterizing trade-off frontiers, but treats per-objective reward models as given and solves weight-selection rather than empirically mapping the compliance-utility-cost frontier (digest N4.6).

title: Efficient Fairness-Performance Pareto Front Computation
why: Computes exact Pareto fronts under classification-style closed-form structure (Bayes-optimal posteriors); contrasts with this paper's premise that open-ended code generation admits no closed form and the compliance-utility frontier must instead be measured empirically (digest N4.7).

title: The Hidden Cost of Readability: How Code Formatting Silently Consumes Your LLM Budget
why: The closest published template for a 'constraint dimension x pass-rate x token-cost' measurement in SE, but studies only one semantically-neutral, removable formatting constraint with no strength sweep (digest N4.8); this paper's core differentiation target.

title: Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models
why: Established checker-based, objectively-verifiable constraint-compliance measurement (the paradigm M3's deterministic checkers descend from) and is named as an external-anchor baseline in digest N8, but has no functional-correctness oracle or cost axis (digest N4.3).

title: FollowBench: A Multi-level Fine-grained Constraint Following Benchmark for Large Language Models
why: Closest existing precedent for a graded constraint-strength ladder (five levels) and is named as an external-anchor baseline in digest N8/N2, but measures NL-instruction satisfaction degradation with no functional-correctness oracle or cost axis (digest N4.3).
